notes: CRITICAL FIX: found and fixed the real, longstanding root cause of the header-alignment bug, which predates this entire session. index_src.html had a genuine duplicate closing inside the Action Planner tab's HTML skeleton (right after #generatedPlanBody), which caused a one-level-too-early cascade: #planTab closed one line early, and the very next closing tag -- which should have closed #planTab -- instead closed .main-content itself. Every tab after Action Planner (including #settingsTab) rendered as a stray DIRECT CHILD of .app-container instead of nested inside .main-content, which broke .main-content's flex width (it measured 0px) and, downstream, the sticky .top-header's width and its header-status child's right-alignment -- exactly the symptom reported (a header button appearing to render 'behind' a tile). Confirmed via a custom Python HTML balance-checker that this exact bug was present before any change made in this session. Fixed by removing the duplicate tag and adding .main-content's/.app-container's own previously-absent closing tags at the true end of the document. Verified live with real resolved computed styles (not just attribute strings): .main-content now measures its correct ~1140px width, .header-status's margin-left resolves to a real positive pixel value pushing it fully right, and .app-container now has exactly 2 children (sidebar, main-content) with all 6 tab views correctly nested inside main-content. index.html (the separate compiled build) was checked and did not have this bug.
